newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq to consider using e-mail.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq to consider using e-mail.

text.p: The governing body of the Nasdaq stock market, which bills itself as the premier stock exchange for high-tech companies, said on Monday it is considering a proposal that would allow brokers to communicate with clients using electronic mail.
Brokerage firms could send order confirmations, proxy materials and customer accounts, as legally required, by e-mail instead of through conventional paper-based mail.

The National Association of Securities Dealers' (NASD) said it voted Friday to submit a rule change that would allow the use of e-mail and would seek comment from investors, securities industries professionals and other groups.

The board also voted to submit a proposal that would help determine the "prevailing market price" on the mark-up of government and other debt securities. The NASD has a rule that dealers must sell debt securities to customers at fair prices.
It will also seek comment concerning what kinds of realted performance information can be used in advertising and selling mutual funds, the NASD said.
